scientific_summary.headline: Model fit identified 6 term(s) with nominal hazard association: age, stage: III vs I, stage: IV vs I +3 more.
strengths: Cox regression was fit with the Efron tie method.
Model estimates use the analyzable cohort after dropping rows with missing selected Cox inputs (N = 342 of 360 outcome-valid rows).

Proportional-hazards checks use the Grambsch-Therneau score test on scaled Schoenfeld residuals versus log time (per term, 1 df, plus a global test); the plot overlay uses LOWESS smoothing for visual inspection only.
The reported discrimination metric is an apparent C-index on the fitted cohort, so it reflects training-cohort ranking only.
A C-index of 0.683 means the fitted model correctly orders approximately 68.3% of evaluable patient pairs by predicted risk.
The overall likelihood-ratio test compares the fitted Cox model with a null model (LR chi-square 92.63, p=1.36e-16).
Global proportional-hazards test (Grambsch-Therneau, log time): chi-square 8.50 on 8 df (p=0.386) across 8 model term(s).
Martingale residual screening is available for continuous covariates not marked categorical: age, biomarker_score, immune_index.
Apparent C-index (training cohort) includes an internal bootstrap percentile 95% CI (0.653 to 0.719) on the fixed fitted risk scores.
cautions: 18 outcome-valid rows (5.0%) were excluded because at least one selected Cox input was missing.
Changing the covariate set can change the analyzable cohort because Cox fitting uses complete-case rows for the selected covariates.
All Cox outputs assume non-informative (independent) censoring.
Competing risks are not modeled in this Cox workflow, so cause-specific questions need dedicated competing-risk methods rather than treating other event types as ordinary censoring.
Left truncation (delayed entry) is not supported; if patients entered the risk set after time 0, coefficient estimates and survival summaries can be biased.
The Cox C-index is apparent, so it is optimistic and should not be treated as external validation.

The reported C-index confidence interval is a bootstrap interval on the same cohort using fixed fitted risk scores, so it understates full model-building uncertainty and does not replace external validation.
The current dashboard does not yet provide a built-in external-cohort apply workflow for Cox validation; validate the final specification on a separate cohort outside this run.
next_steps: Review missingness patterns or use an imputation strategy before treating the fitted cohort as representative.
If martingale LOWESS trends curve strongly away from zero, consider splines, nonlinear transforms, or recoding the continuous covariate.
Interpret hazard ratios together with confidence intervals, not p-values alone.

scientific_summary.headline: Random Survival Forest estimated a holdout C-index of 0.688 on the current evaluation path.
strengths: Random Survival Forest was trained with 7 feature(s) on 480 patients (209 events).
Holdout C-index was estimated on 206 patients (90 events).
Ensemble of 100 trees with min_samples_leaf=6.
Non-parametric model; no proportional-hazards assumption required.
Discrimination was estimated on a deterministic holdout split.
Holdout C-index = 0.688.
IBS = 0.1812 versus a Kaplan-Meier null-model IBS of 0.2115, giving a Brier Skill Score of 0.143.
cautions: A deterministic holdout scores one split, and the point estimate alone does not show its uncertainty; judge it by the bootstrap intervals over the test patients of a model comparison or by repeated cross-validation.
next_steps: Validate on an independent cohort or via cross-validation before drawing clinical conclusions.
Use Brier Skill Score versus the Kaplan-Meier null benchmark, not raw IBS alone, when arguing that a model meaningfully improves survival prediction error.

scientific_summary.headline: DeepSurv estimated a holdout c-index of 0.677 on holdout evaluation.
strengths: DeepSurv trained for 34 epoch(s) on 480 sample(s) (209 events) with 7 features.
Training loss decreased over epochs, indicating successful optimization.
Early stopping picked epoch 34 on a held-out monitor subset of 96 training rows; the reported model was then refit on all 480 training rows for that many epochs.
cautions: Reported C-index is computed on the shared stratified holdout split (480 training and 206 evaluation samples; 30% holdout, identical to the ML comparison for the same seed).

A deterministic holdout scores one split, and the point estimate alone does not show its uncertainty; judge it by the bootstrap intervals over the test patients of a model comparison or by repeated cross-validation.
This DeepSurv path uses full-batch Cox optimization; the batch-size control is recorded for reproducibility but does not change optimization.
Deep-model summaries currently report discrimination (C-index) only; SurvStudio does not yet compute IBS for these paths, so calibration/error comparisons are not symmetric with the ML module.
next_steps: Validate with external data or cross-validation to confirm generalizability.
